questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The culture-difference of France and Denmark

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not easy at all.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Very little - it was very difficult to feel like you where welcome at La Sorbonne, it took me months to even be inscribed at my courses

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Don't get scammed - lot's of people on Facebook etc., who take advantage of students looking for housing in Paris

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That you will know more local people and that is nice!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I did not get any information on how to register, I had to write many e-mails to the administratives and then afterwards to every prof of each course, to ask them to take me on. At Sorbonne, I learned, it depends not even on what faculty, you're at, but also what subject, you're studying, and down to every course - how the registration process is done. This is not very helpfull for a student on exchange, but my experience, talking to the local students, was that Sorbonne in general have many, many problems with their structure and administration.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: e-mails to the administrative office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into the classes I wanted to, but it took me so much time and stress.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: that they get to know an exchange-student, that went before you to the same kind of studies, to get to know the procedure.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Level was not as high as in UCPH, since there was not really any discussions about the texts etc., but more just a walk through of everything.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The pedagogy is very different in UCPH and Sorbonne - at UCPH as a student you are expected to have critical opinions about the stuff, you are reading and learning, and at Sorbonne it was like the prof was a sort of dictator, that you should just learn how to submit to. For me this meant, that it was easier to follow along with understanding everything in French, but it also meant, that the academic level didn't seem very high.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Options Français (pour étudiants
non francophones)
- Intelligence artificielle et objet sociotechniques
- Le corps sous le regard des sociologues-Approches théoriques
- Sociologie des croyances

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Intelligence artificielle et objet sociotechniques. Because this was more interactive and an open learning space. The prof, Laurence Devillers, is critical but still very much listening.

questions.answer: Didn't use any of them

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds - many cultural, sportive and social activities, like cinema, petanque, football, choir etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going to the art museums - they are some of the best in the world and is a nice break from the studies.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going to the Bois de Vincennes!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy! but I have been in France many times, so it was more easy in this way for me.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There is an age difference - the french are much younger, compared to the danish ones.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and welcoming tone and attitude

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Got to know a former exchange student at your designated study
- Remember to use the Crouse -cantine
- Use the modern Bibliotheque Nationale, best open library

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can be nice to connect with a group of your own nationality - like in Cité Univeristé or at the Danish Church

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being in France for a long time

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The communication and administrative part of Sorbonne. Very stressfull experience to go to this school.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Nope. Thank you for the opportunity!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
